topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the framing, objectives, and introductory context for the lecture on cancer evolution and the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Genetic and Epigenetic Mechanisms in Clonal Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how sequential genetic mutations and epigenetic alterations confer competitive growth advantages to drive clonal expansion during tumor evolution.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Cancer Stem Cell Hierarchies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the relationship between normal tissue hierarchies and cancer development, evaluating the evidence for cancer stem cells and cell-of-origin susceptibility in leukemia and colorectal cancer.

topics.label: Role of the Microenvironment and Inflammation in Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how environmental promoters, inflammatory signaling, and stromal co-dependencies create permissive conditions required for mutated cells to expand, progress, and sustain malignancy.

topics.label: Methodologies for Investigating Tumor Evolution and Microenvironments
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the computational, single-cell sequencing, and spatial profiling technologies used to map cancer cell plasticity and microenvironmental interactions in the laboratory.

topics.label: Integrated Evolutionary Framework of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the lecture's core arguments into a unified model showing how mutations, epigenetics, cell of origin, and microenvironmental conditions collectively drive cancer evolution.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Next Steps
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the presentation and provides framing for the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
